newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia won't sell state UES stake in 97 or 98 - Kokh.
newsitem.headline: Russia won't sell state UES stake in 97 or 98 - Kokh.

text.p: Russia is unlikely to sell a 50 percent plus one share government stake in power company Unified Energy System (UES) in either 1997 or 1998, head of the State Property Committee Alfred Kokh said on Wednesday.
"We need to first restructure the company and without the 50 percent (of shares) it cannot be done," said Kokh, whose committee is in charge of the privatisation programme.
"First we need to make the company more effective and then we can start to sell it. I don't think we will sell either this year or next," Kokh said.
A senior government source told journalists on Tuesday that a group of Russian banks had offered to buy the stake from the government this year.

The government owns 52.7 percent of UES, but President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree earlier this month lowering the state's share in the company to 50 percent plus one share and allowing UES to issue convertible bonds on the 2.7 percent stake.
